title: Annotatio VI §.II close: Epitome samples (faith/works, Supper, humanity’s capacity) — stop before §.III
pass_a_gloss: That Faith does not justify without good works, i.e. that solitary Faith does not justify (Antithesis XI to Art. 3, p. m. 560); That good works are necessary to salvation (Antit. I to Art. 4, p. m. 563); That Faith in Christ is not lost, and the Holy Spirit nevertheless dwells in a man, even if he sins knowingly and willingly (that is, in act only, not in habit, and with half-full will) (Ibid., Ant. 3); That Christ’s Body in the Sacred Supper is not taken corporeally together with the bread, but only Bread and Wine are received by mouth, while Christ’s Body is taken spiritually, i.e. by Faith (Antit. 5 to Art. 7, p. m. 574); That the faithful ought not to seek Christ’s Body and blood in the Bread and Wine of the Lord’s Supper, but to lift eyes to Heaven and thence ask Christ’s Body (Ibid. Antith. 15, p. 575); That unbelieving and impenitent Christians in the Lord’s Supper take not the true Body and Blood of Christ but only Bread and wine (Antit. 16, p. m. 575); That Christ according to the Humanity (and so a finite Nature) is altogether incapable of Omnipotence and the other Properties of the Divine Nature (and so of Infinite ones); likewise that to Christ according to the humanity there is indeed given the greatest power in Heaven and on Earth — greater and ampler than all Angels and Creatures received — yet that He has no communication with God’s Omnipotence, nor is divine Omnipotence given to it (i.e. to the human Nature) (Antit. 15 & 16 to Art. 8, p. m. 582).
pass_b_english: That faith does not justify without good works (i.e. solitary faith does not justify); that good works are necessary to salvation; that faith in Christ is not lost and the Spirit still dwells even when someone sins knowingly in act only.

That Christ’s body is not taken corporeally with the bread but only bread and wine by mouth, the body spiritually by faith; that the faithful must look to heaven rather than seek the body in the supper elements; that unbelieving communicants receive only bread and wine.

That Christ according to the humanity is incapable of divine omnipotence and the other infinite properties; that the greatest power given to His humanity still has no communication with God’s omnipotence (Epitome antitheses to Arts. 3–4, 7–8).
Stop before §. III (if Lutherans dropped this acerbic mode / swapped damnations for bare rejections, the door to fraternity would stand open).
source_text: Fidem non justificare sine bonis operibus, i. e. Fidem solitariam non justificare, Antithes. XI. ad Artic. 3. p. m. 560. Bona opera necessaria ad salutem esse, Antit. I. ad Art. 4. p. m. 563. Fidem in Christum non amitti, & Spiritum S. nihilominus in homine habitare, etiamsi sciens volens (puta actu duntaxat, non habitu, & semiplenâ voluntate) peccet homo. Ibidem, Ant. 3. Corpus Christi in S. Coena non corporaliter una cum pane sumi, sed tantum Panem & Vinum ore accipi, Corpus verò Christi spiritualiter, i. e. Fide sumi. Antit. 5. ad Art. 7. p. m. 574. Fideles Corpus & sanguinem Christi non in Pane & Vino Coenae Dominicae quaerere, sed oculos in Coelum attollere, & inde Corpus Christi petere debere. Ibid. Antith. 15. p. 575. Infideles & impaenitentes Christianos in Coena Domini, non verum Corpus & Sanguinem Christi, sed Panem tantum & vinum sumere. Antit. 16. p. m. 575. Christum secundum Humanitatem (eóque finitam Naturam) Omnipotentiae, aliarumque Proprietatum Divinae Naturae (eóque Infinitarum), prorsus non esse capacem. Christo, item, secundum humanitatem, datam quidem maximam potestatem in Coelo & in Terra, videlicet majorem & ampliorem, quàm omnes Angeli & Creaturae acceperunt, sed tamen cum Omnipotentia Dei nullam habere communicationem, neg. Omnipotentiam divinam illi (h. e. humanae Naturae) datam esse, Antit. 15. & 16. ad Art. 8. p. m. 582.
